question.worked_solution:
To evaluate the given expression, we use PEMDAS. 

First, we compute the expression inside the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}(7-5)^{-4}+{(\frac{3}{5}-\frac{1}{2})}^{0} & = \\ {2}^{-4}+{(\frac{6}{10}-\frac{5}{10})}^{0} & = \\ {2}^{-4}+{(\frac{1}{10})}^{0}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that ${(\frac{1}{10})}^{0}=1.$ So, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{-4}+{(\frac{1}{10})}^{0} & = \\ {2}^{-4}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, notice that ${2}^{-4}=\frac{1}{{2}^{4}}=\frac{1}{16}.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{-4}+1 & = \\ \frac{1}{16}+1 & = \\ \frac{1+16}{16} & = \\ \frac{17}{16}. & \end{aligned}
$$
